apiKeys.howToGet: How do I get the API key?

gemini.description: Main engine — generates summaries, tests, flashcards, outlines and everything else. Free tier: 1,500 requests/day.
gemini.step1: Go to aistudio.google.com and sign in with your Google account.
gemini.step2: Click "Get API key" in the left sidebar.
gemini.step3: Press "Create API key" and choose a project (or create a new one).
gemini.step4: Copy the key that appears and paste it in the field above.
gemini.step5: Done. 1,500 requests/day free — more than enough for normal use.

claude.description: Alternative engine — kicks in if Gemini fails or if you prefer to use it as primary. Optional. Requires a payment method on Anthropic.
claude.step1: Go to console.anthropic.com and create an account.
claude.step2: Requires adding a payment method (card). There is initial trial credit.
claude.step3: Go to Settings → API Keys in the sidebar.
claude.step4: Press "Create Key", give it a name and copy the key.
claude.step5: Paste it in the field above and save.

mistral.description: Text fallback if Gemini fails + vision for extracting formulas from scanned PDFs. Optional but recommended.
mistral.step1: Go to console.mistral.ai and create a free account.
mistral.step2: Once inside, go to "API Keys" in the sidebar.
mistral.step3: Press "Create new key", give it a descriptive name.
mistral.step4: Copy the key that appears (shown only once) and paste it above.
mistral.step5: Free tier: monthly token limit, enough for occasional use.

home-1.title: Home — your dashboard
home-1.body: Upload a new document, check your upcoming exams, and quickly access the rest of the app — this is the first screen you see when you log in.

home-2.title: Upload your first document
home-2.body: Drag a PDF or a photo of your notes into the box above (or use the buttons), without needing to go to the Library first. If you upload 2 or more PDFs at once, it offers to generate a combined summary of all of them.

home-3.title: Upcoming exams
home-3.body: Add an exam date directly from here (with optional subject and color) and you’ll see it listed with a countdown — it’s the same reminder that appears in the Calendar.

home-4.title: Documents, Subjects, Flashcards, and Streak
home-4.body: The 4 cards at the top are quick shortcuts: Documents and Subjects take you to the Library, Flashcards today to Pending, and Streak to Progress.

home-5.title: Subject mastery
home-5.body: As soon as you start reviewing flashcards, a progress bar by subject appears here, calculated from your actual correct answers — so you can see at a glance what you’ve mastered.

library-1.title: Library — your notes and PDFs
library-1.body: Upload your notes (PDF, photo, or text) and organize them by Subject and Topic. When you open a document, you can generate summaries, outlines, flashcards, exams, podcasts, and more.

library-subjects.title: Subjects and Topics
library-subjects.body: Create a subject and group documents by Topic within it. You can drag a document onto a subject or topic to reassign it at any time.

library-upload.title: Import PDFs
library-upload.body: Upload one or multiple PDFs with this button, or drag them directly onto the document list.

library-tabs.title: Documents, Summaries, and Study Plans
library-tabs.body: Besides the document list, there are two more tabs in the side menu: "Saved summaries" (those you’ve saved with 💾) and "Study plans" (with their progress).

library-multiselect.title: Multi-select
library-multiselect.body: Check multiple documents with the boxes, and a bar appears at the bottom with 4 options: combined summary, combined flashcards, combined exam, and joint study plan — useful before an exam that covers multiple topics.

library-plan.title: Joint study plan
library-plan.body: Set an exam date and your available weekly study hours (Settings → Study availability), and the AI schedules the topics day by day. If you set a date, it also creates a reminder in your Calendar automatically.

library-podcast.title: Notes podcast
library-podcast.body: In any document or saved summary, there’s a headphones icon — generate a narrated podcast you can download or send to "My podcasts" on your phone to listen offline. Available on desktop, web, and also in MyStudy Scan.

library-dudas.title: Amber words and underlining
library-dudas.body: In a scanned document, the text respects what you underlined by hand, and words that weren’t read with certainty appear in amber: tap them to correct or confirm. It works the same as MyStudy App’s notebook, so you don’t have to learn it twice.

library-sync.title: Cloud sync (desktop)
library-sync.body: In the desktop app, each document shows an icon: amber if it’s only on this computer (tap to upload), green if it’s also in the cloud.

cuaderno-1.title: MyStudy App Notebook — your notes, neat and tidy
cuaderno-1.body: Take a photo of your notebook page, and it’s added to the notes for that subject under today’s date. Day by day, a full notebook builds up instead of scattered photos.

cuaderno-2.title: Choose subject and add the page
cuaderno-2.body: You always choose the subject (the topic is optional), so nothing ends up in the wrong folder. Tap "Add notebook page" — on mobile, the camera opens directly. The photo isn’t saved: only the text remains.

cuaderno-3.title: The amber words
cuaderno-3.body: Handwriting isn’t always read with certainty. Unclear words appear in amber: tap to confirm or correct them. What you underlined in your notebook stays underlined, and formulas and roots appear as they should, not in code.

cuaderno-4.title: Edit with the pen
cuaderno-4.body: The pen icon, next to the date, opens the note for editing. You have bold, italics, underline, strikethrough, headings, and lists — and you see the formatting applied as you type, not with odd symbols. Formulas are drawn; double-click one to turn it back into text and fix it.

cuaderno-5.title: Print, Word, and study
cuaderno-5.body: With the notebook open, you have the printer (which also saves as PDF) and the download for Word, keeping your formatting. And "Study" opens it like any other document: summary, flashcards, exam, and podcast based on your own notes.

cuaderno-6.title: On mobile
cuaderno-6.body: In MyStudy App, you have this same screen, including the pen tool. In MyStudy Scan, the "MyStudy App Notebook" button on the home screen opens the camera directly to add today’s page — scan it in class and review it later anywhere.

study-1.title: Pending — everything left to do
study-1.body: A single dashboard with cards: flashcards to review today, subjects with no exams done yet, notes you haven’t worked on, how much is left for your weekly goal, and the % remaining of any active study plan.

study-2.title: Review with flashcards (SM-2)
study-2.body: Tap the flashcards card to see only the ones due today based on the spaced repetition schedule — not your entire deck. If you get it right, it’ll take longer to reappear; if you miss it, it’ll come back soon.

study-3.title: Study mode
study-3.body: Tap the card (or Space) to flip it and see the answer, then mark if you got it right with the buttons "Again / Hard / Good / Easy" (or keys 1-4) — this way, the system adjusts when to ask you again.

study-4.title: Explanation, not just the answer
study-4.body: The back of each flashcard can include a hint and a brief explanation of why, not just the correct answer, so you understand the concept instead of just memorizing it.

exam-1.title: Exam — choose a document
exam-1.body: This screen is just the starting point: pick the document you want to be tested on, and you’ll enter it to generate the exam. (For an exam combining multiple documents at once, do it from the Library with multi-select.)

exam-2.title: Available exam types
exam-2.body: Inside the document, under the "Assessment" group, you can choose: quiz, written response, solved problems, adaptive (focuses on your real weak spots), or a timed mock exam.

exam-3.title: Automatic grading
exam-3.body: When you finish, it grades itself and gives you your score instantly, with the correct answer explained for every question you missed.

exam-4.title: History
exam-4.body: All your completed exams are saved, and you can check your grade progress in Progress.

tutor-1.title: Tutor — learn by chatting
tutor-1.body: Type or talk to the Tutor about any question. At the top, you can pick a document from your Library as context or leave it on "free topic."

tutor-mic.title: Voice mode
tutor-mic.body: Tap the microphone for a voice conversation — the Tutor listens, responds out loud, and you can interrupt by speaking anytime (it detects your voice even while it’s talking).

tutor-socratic.title: Guided mode (Socratic)
tutor-socratic.body: Turn it on so the Tutor asks you questions to help you find the answer yourself instead of giving it to you directly — like a private teacher. If you get stuck, you can ask for the answer.

tutor-board.title: Whiteboard
tutor-board.body: The Tutor can draw diagrams, formulas, and outlines on a side whiteboard (expandable to full screen). You can also draw on it with the pen.

tutor-history.title: Session history
tutor-history.body: Every conversation saves automatically as you talk — tap the clock (at the top) to resume a previous session or the pen to start a new one.

languages-1.title: Languages — practice every day
languages-1.body: Choose from 12 languages, your level (A1 to C2, the official European scale), and a conversation topic (travel, work, food, tech...).

languages-mode.title: Written, speaking, or listening practice
languages-mode.body: Written mode: text exercises (fill in the blanks, translate, conjugate...). Speaking mode: talk to a native tutor by voice. Listening mode: listen to generated audios and answer questions.

languages-vocab.title: Your own vocabulary
languages-vocab.body: Upload your own vocabulary lists (from class or a book), and they’ll be used to create personalized exercises and exams with that material.

languages-exam.title: Full language exam
languages-exam.body: Besides practicing, you can generate a full exam with automatic grading and a final score.

lecture-1.title: Voice notes — record while studying
lecture-1.body: Pick a subject (optional) and record your notes by speaking. They’re transcribed automatically, and a summary with key points is generated when you finish.

lecture-recorder.title: Recording panel
lecture-recorder.body: Turn on "Remove noise and interruptions" if you’re recording in a noisy or long session — it automatically filters out unrelated content. When you stop, the notes save to your Library.

lecture-recent.title: Recent notes
lecture-recent.body: The right panel lists your latest voice notes — tap one to open it directly in the Library.

solve-1.title: Solve a photographed exercise
solve-1.body: Take a photo or upload an image of an exercise (math, physics, chemistry...) and get a step-by-step solution instantly — no need to save it as a document first.

solve-2.title: Save it if it helps
solve-2.body: If you want to review it later, save the solution to your Library when you're done — and see it listed under "Recent" on this same screen.

compare-1.title: Compare two documents
compare-1.body: Choose document A and B, and the mode: only differences, only similarities, or both — useful for comparing your notes with the textbook, or two exams from different years.

stats-1.title: Progress — your study stats
stats-1.body: Cards showing flashcards reviewed, exams completed, average grade, and your streak of consecutive study days.

stats-2.title: Activity and grade trends
stats-2.body: One graph shows your recent study activity, and another tracks how your exam grades have changed over time.

stats-3.title: Weak areas and time per subject
stats-3.body: One section highlights the specific topics you struggle with most (so you know where to focus), and another shows how much time you’ve spent on each subject.

calendar-1.title: Calendar — never miss an exam
calendar-1.body: Monthly view with navigation between months and a "Today" button. Tap "+ Add event" or any day to create an exam reminder, with its own subject and color.

calendar-2.title: Reminders before exams
calendar-2.body: Get a notification (on your phone or browser) a few days before, so it doesn’t sneak up on you.

calendar-3.title: Study plans appear too
calendar-3.body: If you generate a study plan from the Library with an exam date, the reminder is added here automatically — no need to create it twice.

settings-1.title: Appearance and languages
settings-1.body: Change the visual theme, voice and reading speed for text-to-speech, the interface language (Español/English/Deutsch/Français), and the language the AI uses for summaries/flashcards/exams — these are two separate settings.

settings-2.title: Study availability
settings-2.body: Set how many hours you can study each day of the week — the study plan (Library) uses this to distribute topics realistically. You can adjust these before generating each plan.

settings-3.title: Exam reminders
settings-3.body: Turn exam notifications on or off, and choose how many days in advance you want to be reminded.

settings-plan.title: Plan and billing
settings-plan.body: Here you’ll see your plan (Free, Trial, or Pro) and your monthly usage: generations, podcasts, transcription minutes, and scanned pages are tracked separately. You can upgrade to Pro, buy extra credits if you run out, or manage your subscription and invoices.

settings-retencion.title: What’s saved and what’s auto-deleted
settings-retencion.body: Original files you upload (PDF or photo) and solved exercises are deleted after 10 days — download them if you want to keep them. Your summaries, flashcards, and exams are saved forever. With "Course Archive," you can save or restore a full backup of an entire course.

settings-4.title: Your account and data
settings-4.body: Change your name or password, manage backups (on desktop, including Whisper settings for local transcription), or delete your account if needed.
